<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915585_theRebbe_828" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915585_theRebbe_828__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Both opinions are true because they have their root in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof, which contains two aspects: being infinitely above and infinitely below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is explained in the discourses,</t>
    <t s="2">that both opinions are true,</t>
    <t s="3">for both have their root in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="4">for in Ein Sof there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="5">That He is above, above, without end,</t>
    <t s="6">and that He is below, below, without limit.</t>
    <t s="7">And these two matters are the root of the lower knowledge and the higher knowledge.</t>
    <t s="8">For from the aspect of the revelation of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="9">which is revealed in every place below, below without limit,</t>
    <t s="10">everything before Him is considered as nothing — this is the higher knowledge that "below there is nothing."</t>
    <t s="11">And from the aspect of the concealment of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="12">which is elevated in His Awtsmoos above, above without end,</t>
    <t s="13">the creations exist as a tangible entity — this is the lower knowledge that "below there is something."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>It must be understood how the lower knowledge, rooted in the concealment of Ein Sof, is perfected by the revelation of the higher knowledge, and why it is still considered true.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one must understand,</t>
    <t s="1">that since even the lower knowledge has its root in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="2">the perfection of the lower knowledge would seemingly be that within it there should be a revelation that "below there is something"</t>
    <t s="3">(not that the creations are a tangible entity from their own perspective,</t>
    <t s="4">but rather)</t>
    <t s="5">because Ein Sof is above, above without end,</t>
    <t s="6">and in the discourses it is explained,</t>
    <t s="7">that the perfection of the lower knowledge comes about through the revelation of the higher knowledge shining within it.</t>
    <t s="8">Also, one must understand on the other hand,</t>
    <t s="9">regarding what is said in the discourses that even the lower knowledge is true because it has a root in the Awtsmoos of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="10">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="11">since the matter of "above, above without end"</t>
    <t s="12">(the root of the lower knowledge)</t>
    <t s="13">is the concealment of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="14">the perception that "below there is something"</t>
    <t s="15">(as is perceived in the lower knowledge)</t>
    <t s="16">is seemingly not from the aspect of Ein Sof, but rather on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="17">because Ein Sof is not perceived within it,</t>
    <t s="18">and nevertheless they say,</t>
    <t s="19">that the opinion that "below there is something"</t>
    <t s="20">(as it is in the lower knowledge)</t>
    <t s="21">is a true opinion.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The explanation of the term "nature" is discussed, with several interpretations: that it is a new name for constant miracles, that it derives from the word for a coin stamp, or that it refers to something without reason or intellect.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="2">that it is explained in the discourses,</t>
    <t s="3">that the term "nature" has several interpretations.</t>
    <t s="4">For in the Responsa of the Chacham Tzvi</t>
    <t s="5">it is stated,</t>
    <t s="6">that the name "nature" is a new term coined by the later sages.</t>
    <t s="7">For since everything</t>
    <t s="8">(even nature)</t>
    <t s="9">is from Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="10">therefore even nature is a miracle.</t>
    <t s="11">Except that these miracles are constant,</t>
    <t s="12">continuous miracles.</t>
    <t s="13">And there are those who say</t>
    <t s="14">that "nature" (teva) is from the word "coin" (matbea).</t>
    <t s="15">For it is stated in the Mishnah,</t>
    <t s="16">A person strikes many coins with one seal, and they all resemble one another,</t>
    <t s="17">but the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, stamped every person with the seal of Adam the first man, yet not one of them resembles another.</t>
    <t s="18">And in the Tanya</t>
    <t s="19">it is stated,</t>
    <t s="20">that "nature" is a borrowed term for anything that is not according to reason and intellect.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
